# Recommend recovery-first silent-continue strategy

## Summary

Recommend a proxy-side recovery-first strategy ("try to recover silently, re-route to the next healthy provider") with safe/unsafe windows around the content-delivered boundary, bounded retries, and per-provider cooldowns — quantified from the Aug 3 logs.

## User stories

- As an operator, when an upstream provider fails mid-stream, I want the proxy to first try to continue automatically so my session does not stop and I do not have to type "continue".

## Acceptance Criteria

- Recommendation defines safe vs unsafe recovery windows relative to the content-delivered boundary (LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C): when re-routing mid-stream is safe (no assistant content / tool calls delivered) vs unsafe (content already sent to the client).
- Recommendation specifies bounded retry/re-route attempt counts and per-provider cooldown / circuit-breaker rules (reusing existing Tier-2/Tier-3 mechanisms) to avoid recovery loops masking persistent failures.
- Recommendation escalates to an informative error after recovery is exhausted.
- Recommendation quantifies from Aug 3 logs how many of the 98 client-visible stream errors would have been avoided under this strategy (with the boundary caveat stated).
- Recommendation confirms the strategy fits the existing architecture (`proxy/proxy/provider.py` `proxy_with_remote_fallback()`, config-driven provider chains) and requires no client-side changes.
- Identifies the follow-up implementation work item(s) the recommendation implies.

## Minimal Implementation

- Use F2 taxonomy + F3 site audit as evidence.
- Draft the recommendation section (safe/unsafe windows, bounded attempts, cooldowns, escalation) with quantified impact and architecture fit.
- Commit the section into the analysis report; create the follow-up work-item spec.

## Dependencies

- Children: Aug 3 error taxonomy & root-cause report; Audit synthetic SSE finish_reason:error sites.

## Deliverables

- Recommendation section in the analysis report + follow-up implementation work-item spec.

# Recommend informative-error SSE fallback

## Summary

Recommend enriching the synthetic SSE error event (or equivalent non-SSE error response) with a structured payload — `type`, `message`, provider, model, suggested action — used only when recovery is impossible, so the client gets an informative error instead of an unspecified one.

## User stories

- As an operator, when recovery is genuinely impossible, I want an informative error (type + message + provider + suggested action) so I can understand and act instead of seeing an unspecified error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Recommendation proposes a concrete structured payload schema for the synthetic SSE event: fields for error `type`, `message`, provider, model, and suggested action (or an equivalent non-SSE error JSON shape).
- Recommendation defines the trigger conditions: recovery exhausted (retry/re-route chain done) or content already delivered (unsafe to re-route) — i.e. used only when recovery is impossible.
- Recommendation verifies backward compatibility: no client-side change required; existing clients still receive `finish_reason: error` but now with an informative `error` field.
- Recommendation quantifies from the Aug 3 logs how many client-visible errors would have carried the enriched payload (the complement of the recovery-first avoidance number).
- Identifies the follow-up implementation work item(s), including the minimal enrichment points from the site audit.

## Minimal Implementation

- Use F3 site audit to identify the single best enrichment point(s).
- Draft the schema and fallback trigger rules; state compatibility and quantified coverage.
- Commit the recommendation section; create the follow-up work-item spec.

## Dependencies

- Child: Audit synthetic SSE finish_reason:error sites.

## Deliverables

- Recommendation section (schema + triggers + compatibility) in the analysis report + follow-up implementation work-item spec.
